newsitem.title: USA: GM cautious on China car plant start up.
newsitem.headline: GM cautious on China car plant start up.

text.p: General Motors Corp Chairman Jack Smith said Thursday GM's mid-size car production venture in Shanghai may not start volume production until April 1999 because of longer-than-expected negotiatons to obtain final goverment approval.
Smith said GM probably does not have enough to time to complete construction of the plant to meet the previously scheduled production launch of December 1998.
"Internally, we're saying April of 1999," Smith said at a breakfast meeting with reporters Thursday.

GM and Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp will each own 50 percent of the more than $1 billion joint venture, called Shanghai General Motors Corp. It will eventually have capacity to produce 100,000 Buick-based sedans a year.

Smith said GM may still hold some opening ceremonies for the plant in December 1998 to satisfy local officials. Those officials have been adamant about starting production on the original date, despite it taking longer than expected to hammer out final details of the project.
"They have never given up on that date, but its December of next year," he said.
Nonetheless, Smith said construction work on the plant is continuing 24 hours a day in an effort to meet the schedule.
Smith also said the Shanghai plant will have the capability to build minivans because the cars produced there share the same basic platform as GM's new U.S. built minivans.
"We'd love to do that, but we'd have to get permission" from the Chinese government, Smith said.
